_readme: THE FROZEN IDENTIFIERS. This file is COMMITTED. config/product.json is not.
That asymmetry is the whole point. The freeze check compares the identifiers in your
product.json against this lock. Before this file existed the check compared product.json
against its own previous commit — and since product.json is never committed, `git show`
returned nothing and the check skipped, silently, on every run. The rule its own docstring
called 'the check that matters' had never once executed.
These values are written into data your customers already hold, and into artifacts you
have already signed:
jwtIssuer        change it and every live session and refresh token is rejected
linkNs           change it and every share link you have ever sent stops resolving
signatureDomain  change it and every signed artifact fails verification, forever
eventNs          change it and consumers filtering on the old namespace go deaf
userAgent        change it and whoever allow-listed you stops seeing you
TO REBRAND: edit `identity` and `brand` in product.json. Leave these alone.
To change one anyway: edit BOTH product.json and this lock, and put a line beginning
'MIGRATION:' in the commit body saying why and what the compatibility window is. The
versioned identifiers (linkNs, signatureDomain) may only move forward by bumping the
suffix — acme.link.v1 -> acme.link.v2 — never by editing the stem, so that old artifacts
keep verifying against the old value.
Empty strings below mean 'not yet chosen'. Fill them when you fill product.json; from that
commit on, they are frozen.
